newsitem.title: GERMANY: Commerzbank pleased with telebanking unit.
newsitem.headline: Commerzbank pleased with telebanking unit.

text.p: Commerzbank AG said on Tuesday its telephone banking unit Comdirect was running according to plan, despite incurring a 46 million marks ($26.8 million) operating loss in 1996, up from 42 million in 1995.
Chief executive Martin Kohlhaussen told a news conference that he was still expecting the unit to turn a profit in 1999.

Comdirect, which was established in early 1995 and forms part of a strong trend in Germany towards branchless banking, now has more than 80,000 customers, up from 60,000 in mid-1996, Kohlhaussen said.
"We are thoroughly happy with that development," he said of the 1996 loss. "It is totally according to plan."

In it annual report which was released on Tuesday, Commerzbank also said that some 30,000 of the 75,000 Comdirect clients at end-1996 were using its discount brokerage facilities, making the unit the market leader in this area.
The negative operating result was due to the persistently high cost of technical infrastructure and acquiring clients, the bank said.
